title: The 15M: First Directional Break
hook: BOS #1 is where the sequence starts, and it has to close on the 15M.

launchpad.outcome: Identify BOS #1 as a 15M candle close through the 15M level in the direction of the HTF story, and explain why BOS #1 is not an entry.
launchpad.missionQuestion: What has to happen on the 15M before the sequence can start?

takeaways: BOS #1 is a 15M directional break, or a qualifying MSS.
It needs a 15M candle close. A wick doesn’t count.
A correction toward the original 15M break is preferred. A reclaim of the level is extra confirmation, not a requirement.
Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 occurred.
remember: BOS #1 = A 15M CLOSE. NOT A WICK. NOT AN ENTRY.

slides.headline: The sequence starts on the 15M.
slides.line: BOS (break of structure) #1 is the first directional break. It happens on the 15-minute chart.

slides.headline: A close counts. A wick doesn’t.
slides.line: BOS #1 needs a 15M candle to close through the 15M level.

versus.label: Counts as BOS #1
points: A 15M candle closes through the 15M level.
The break is in the direction of the HTF (higher timeframe) story.

versus.label: Doesn’t count
points: A wick pokes through, and the candle closes back.

check.prompt: A 15M candle wicks above the level, then closes back below it. Is that BOS #1?

options.label: Yes, price traded above it
options.feedback: Wicks don’t count. BOS #1 needs a 15M candle close through the level.

options.label: No, it didn’t close above
options.why: Right. BOS #1 is confirmed by a 15M candle close, not a wick.

slides.headline: Watch BOS #1 close on the 15M.
slides.line: Bullish example. The HTF story is bullish. Press the button to print each 15M candle.

steps.caption: Price is pushing higher. No 15M candle has closed above the 15M level yet.
BOS #1. This 15M candle closes above the 15M level, in the direction of the HTF story.
BOS #1 starts the sequence. It isn’t an entry. Next, the 5M has to build the rest.
BOS #1 can also be a qualifying MSS (market structure shift) on the 15M. It counts only when it agrees with the HTF ICC direction.

check.prompt: BOS #1 just closed. What do you do next?

options.label: Enter now, the break is strong
options.feedback: Don’t enter simply because BOS #1 occurred. The 5M still has to build Correction #1, BOS #2, Correction #2 and BOS #3.

options.label: Switch to the 5M and wait for the sequence
options.why: Right. BOS #1 starts the sequence. The 5M builds the rest.

slides.kicker: Step 3 · The 15M level after the break
slides.headline: The 15M break level still matters.
slides.line: Tap each card. This rule is conditional and still being tested.

cards.label: Preferred
cards.sub: The correction after BOS #1 comes back toward the original 15M break.

cards.label: Extra confirmation
cards.sub: A reclaim of the 15M BOS or MSS level can add structural confirmation.

cards.label: Not mandatory
cards.sub: Don’t reject an otherwise valid setup just because a reclaim didn’t happen.

slides.headline: Bearish story. Find BOS #1.
slides.line: The HTF story is bearish. The 15M level is the low of the third 15M candle, the small one. Find the first 15M candle that closes below it.
slides.ask: Tap the 15M candle that is BOS #1.
slides.why: That’s the first 15M candle to close below the 15M level. That close is BOS #1.

after.caption: BOS #1. A 15M close below the level, with the bearish story. Now the 5M takes over.

slides.quote: BOS #1 starts the sequence. It doesn’t start the trade.

slides.prompt: In your own words, what counts as BOS #1, and why isn’t it an entry?
slides.modelAnswer: BOS #1 is a 15M directional break, or a qualifying MSS, in the direction of the HTF story, and it needs a 15M candle close, not a wick. It only starts the sequence. I still wait for the 5M to build Correction #1, BOS #2, Correction #2, BOS #3 and the retest.
